# Lindela Lite

> Open-source climate-conflict and flood-impact toolkit. Ingests public data,
> normalizes it into simple schemas, computes transparent baseline risk scores,
> and serves them over an HTTP API with a no-build frontend.

This file is the map an agent needs to work in this repository without reading
all 28,000 lines. It is a map, not a summary — where a claim here matters, the
source file is the authority.

- Package: `@lindela/lite`, private, MIT, Node >= 20, ESM throughout.
- Runtime dependencies: `pg` and nothing else. `npm test` needs no database.
- Single process, single port (`LINDELA_LITE_PORT` or 4177), single Postgres
  table (`lite_records`) or a single JSON file.

## Verify before you claim

```bash
npm test              # node --test test/*.test.js
npm run validate      # OpenAPI endpoint presence, model-basis status,
                      # capability guard, i18n completeness
npm run test:coverage # thresholds: lines 75, branches 60, functions 75
```

`validate` checks that a hand-maintained endpoint list in `scripts/validate.mjs`
is present in `docs/openapi.yaml`. It does **not** derive that list from the
router, so a route added without a spec entry passes. It also does not check
internal doc links.

`npm test` and `npm run validate` must both exit 0. Never gate a check on a
pipe (`npm test | tail -5`) — `tail` masks the exit code and truncates the
pass/fail summary, which is the last line. Redirect to a file and read it.

## The rule that governs the whole codebase

**Flood probability here is empirical co-occurrence, not hydrology.** It is not
a return period, not a recurrence interval, not an annual exceedance
probability. Any of that vocabulary appearing in the tree fails the build via
`scripts/check-no-flood-probability.mjs`, which scans `src/`, `public/`,
`scripts/`, `test/`, and `docs/`. The one permitted exception is
`docs/flood-probability-model-basis.md`.

This extends into the payload contract:

- Risk "percentiles" are **sensitivity bands**. They were renamed so they would
  stop reading as quantiles.
- `false_alert: null` means *not determined*, not zero.
- A missing forecast is not a 0% chance of rain.
- `0` and `null` are different. A coordinate at 0° is a coordinate. Use
  `Number.isFinite(Number(x))`, never truthiness, on nullable numerics.

When you add a numeric output, ask what qualification the docs carry and whether
it reaches the caller. Half of them historically did not.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `src/server.js` | The router. ~2,700 lines, every `/api/v1/*` route. |
| `src/store.js` | `JsonStore` + the `COLLECTIONS` list every store keys off. |
| `src/postgres-store.js` | `PostgresStore`. Same contract, different backend. |
| `src/schema.js` | Normalized record shapes and `emptyStore()`. |
| `src/ingestion.js` | `runIngestion`, `OUTPUT_COLLECTIONS`, source policies. |
| `src/connectors/` | 17 connectors; `spec.js` is the SDK (`defineConnector`). |
| `src/analytics/` | Flood probability, impact, downscaling, ensemble. |
| `public/` | Eight PWA surfaces. No framework, no build step, no bundler. |
| `test/` | `node:test`. `store-conformance.test.js` runs one contract against every backend. |
| `docs/` | Architecture, OpenAPI, improvements audit, model basis. |

## Three lists that must agree

`COLLECTIONS` (store), `OUTPUT_COLLECTIONS` (ingestion), `emptyStore()`
(schema). When they drift, records vanish with no error anywhere: the producer
writes them, the consumer never asks for them, and every number still looks
plausible.

The same class of bug has appeared four times in this repository. Guard it with
behaviour — assert that a stub connector's records come back out of the store —
never by grepping source text for a collection name. Two guards that did exactly
that passed with the bug fully present.

## Storage backends

Four modes via `LINDELA_LITE_DB_MODE`: `auto`, `postgres`, `pg0`, `json`.
`postgres` and `pg0` are the same `PostgresStore`; `auto` prefers Postgres if
`DATABASE_URL` is set, then pg0, then JSON.

The two backends must agree. `JsonStore.replaceAnalytics` stores six derived
collections; `PostgresStore`'s once took four, so the impact figures were
computed and silently dropped on Postgres alone. `test/store-conformance.test.js`
is what makes that class of divergence impossible to reintroduce — it needs
`LINDELA_LITE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set to exercise the Postgres half.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, jobs `test`, `coverage`, `audit`, `sbom`,
`live-sources`, `dashboard`, and `provenance` (tag pushes only, gated on the
first four).

**There is no Postgres in CI.** No job sets `LINDELA_LITE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, so
`test/store-conformance.test.js` runs its Postgres half as a silent skip and
`src/postgres-store.js` sits near 0% function coverage in the coverage gate —
on the backend every production deployment selects. Treat that as a known gap,
not as a passing test.

## Conventions

- Node package; the Python conventions in the surrounding `CLAUDE.md` do not apply.
- Tests use `node:test`. No mocking — real objects, real local HTTP server.
- Records are keyed on `id`, minted by `stableId(prefix, parts)`.
- Every connector declares a `rateLimit` in its policy. Whether it is *enforced*
  is a separate question — check, do not assume.
